change_note: Raised by the inferred-household programme. A better-evidenced named building substitutes for this roof rather than standing beside it.

placement.position_note: INTERPRETIVE PLACEMENT, NOT A RECOVERED LOT. A second shanty on the same ground. The band follows ROADMAP K1's placement rule - businesses toward the river and the built streets, residences further out - using the same frontage bands the reconstruction recipes already work in, which come from the 80 ft platted street module in data/traces/street_control.json. The centre was tested against every structure footprint in the dataset, against the reserved slots of the two uninstantiated phase-2 recipes, against the platted street corridors of the K7 block grid so that no invented building stands in the roadway, and against the committed heightfield for coverage, dry ground and step tolerance; it is free ground and nothing more. The dataset's 20 m working georeference uncertainty applies on top of an already invented position.

residents.name: The Bacon household — a reconstructed labourer (north division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. inf_labourer_shanty_north_b is a structure record this parcel raises for the purpose, because no roof of the right family stood free in this district. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: THIS BUILDING IS IN THE MODEL BECAUSE OF THIS HOUSEHOLD. Neither is documented: the household is inferred from the town's demonstrable needs and the roof was raised to house it. Its existence, position and size are all inventions, and the chips above say so.

persons.name: Willard Bacon
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE TENTH OF 14 LABOURER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. THE LARGEST TRADE IN ANY WESTERN TOWN AND THE ONE NO ROSTER RECORDS, because a labourer advertises nothing, holds no office and joins no church committee - the three ways almost every documented person in this dataset became documented. The harbour works were under construction through 1834 and 1835 (both piers are structure records here), the streets were being graded, and several hundred buildings were being raised. Twelve labouring households are inferred - the largest single group in this layer and still a small fraction of what 3,265 people implies - and every one of them is housed in the meanest roof the schedule carries: a D1 log cabin or a D2 plank shanty. ONE FURTHER LABOURING HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-14, ON THE SAME TERMS AND FOR THE SAME REASON. The count above calls itself a small fraction of what 3,265 people implies, so it is a floor by its own text, and twelve was where method rule 5 stopped it: another household needed another roof. The Randolph and Wells block parcel has since put a D1 log cabin on the plat in the South Division, which is the family this layer houses every one of its eight adopted labourers in and the meanest roof the schedule carries. Thirteen labouring households are inferred. The arithmetic against the 1835 census is unchanged; what changed is that a roof exists to hold one more of the households that arithmetic already implied. ONE FURTHER LABOURING HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-14, ON THE TERMS METHOD RULE 6 SETS AND FOR THE SAME REASON AS THE THIRTEENTH. The count above calls itself a small fraction of what 3,265 people implies, so it is a floor by its own text, and thirteen was where method rule 5 stopped it: another household needed another roof. The block parcel at Randolph and Clinton has since put a D1 log cabin on the plat in the WEST Division - the meanest roof the schedule carries, the family this layer houses nine of its eleven housed labourers in, and the first anonymous roof of that family to stand west of the river. This layer already places two labouring households in the West Division, in raised D2 plank shanties, so the adoption moves no trade across a division line that this programme had not already argued: it houses the fourteenth labourer in a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted instead of raising a fifteenth building. Fourteen labouring households are inferred. The arithmetic against the 1835 census is unchanged.

METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, RAISED FOR A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). A second shanty on the same ground. It is NOT one of the anonymous count-units of the 665-roof programme: those are placed by aggregate mix and carry no occupant, while this one exists because the occupation census says the town held a household of this trade and no anonymous roof of the right family stood free in this district. It consumes one slot of its district's programme target rather than adding to it - see the accounting block in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json.
